stem: A client has hematuria with red blood cell casts, elevated blood pressure, and proteinuria that is not in the nephrotic range. Which renal syndrome is most consistent with these findings?
rationale: NCBI StatPearls describes nephritic syndrome as a glomerular inflammatory syndrome characterized by hematuria, elevated blood pressure, variable proteinuria, and the appearance of red blood cell casts. Proteinuria is typically below the nephrotic range. Therefore B is the best answer. A is characterized primarily by heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia. C is more typically associated with tubular epithelial or granular casts rather than the nephritic combination of RBC casts, hematuria, and hypertension. D can produce pyuria and white blood cell casts but does not characteristically produce this glomerular nephritic pattern.
educational_objective: Recognize nephritic syndrome by glomerular hematuria/RBC casts with hypertension and usually sub-nephrotic proteinuria, and distinguish it from nephrotic and tubulointerstitial patterns.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine — NCBI Bookshelf
source_version_date: Nephritic Syndrome last updated 2023-08-08; current NCBI pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Nephritic Syndrome > Introduction: hematuria, elevated BP, decreased urine output/edema with glomerular inflammation, RBC casts and variable proteinuria. Nephritic Syndrome > History and Physical: hematuria, non-nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypertension and renal insufficiency. Urinalysis > Casts: RBC casts are associated with glomerulonephritis/intrinsic glomerular disease; WBC casts with pyelonephritis/interstitial inflammation; epithelial/granular casts with tubular injury among other renal processes.
source_claim_supported: Hematuria with RBC casts, hypertension and usually sub-nephrotic proteinuria is a nephritic pattern reflecting glomerular inflammation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed page 14, Physiological Adaptation: 'Identify pathophysiology related to an acute or chronic condition' and recognize signs and symptoms of client complications.
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — nephritic syndrome/glomerular inflammation recognition
correction_summary: Replaced generic NCBI sourcing and filler alternatives with exact nephritic-syndrome and urinalysis locators and genuine renal differential patterns. Reworded 'mild proteinuria' to the source-supported and clinically meaningful 'not in the nephrotic range.'
audit_findings: The source directly supports hematuria, RBC casts, hypertension and usually sub-nephrotic proteinuria in nephritic syndrome. A-D audit: B uniquely explains the entire glomerular pattern; A conflicts with the absence of nephrotic-range protein loss and lacks the characteristic RBC-cast emphasis; C and D have different cast/urinalysis patterns. No diagnosis synonymous with nephritic glomerulonephritis was used as a distractor, avoiding a second defensible answer. Blueprint is a direct NCSBN 2026 Physiological Adaptation pathophysiology match. Independent adversarial second pass found no ambiguity, cueing, filler, or unsupported precision.
